analysis.title: Industrial Metals Weekly: Negative risk tone weighs on copper equities
key_insights: Copper equities fell 7% w/w while spot copper was relatively flat, driven by a 3.7% US inflation print and an AI-led equity selloff.
Chilean labour risk has cleared: Escondida supervisors ratified a 36-month contract on October 14, and Centinela's two unions ratified a deal on Sunday, ending a strike of more than a week.
With the labour premium removed, focus shifts to other supply problems, including Codelco's partial suspension at El Teniente after a landslide killed two contractors.
Metal is being diverted to the US, and Codelco is offering copper to European customers at a record premium of $350/tonne, which RBC says shows tightness in the physical market.
Singapore iron ore futures dipped below $90/t for the first time in two years on soft steel demand and strong supply, then firmed on the seasonal pick-up in steel production (CRU).
Vale's CEO estimates higher energy and freight costs have made ~10% of seaborne supply, roughly 160Mt, unprofitable, which should support a price recovery (mining.com).
Weekly moves: copper -0.6% to $6.62/lb, nickel -2.4% to $6.88/lb, zinc -2.6% to $1.70/lb, met coal -0.4% to $267.7/mt, iron ore +0.7% to $90.90/dmt.

Chart of the Week: junior copper developers have re-rated roughly 2-3x since 2023. EV/lb jumped from $0.04 to $0.08-0.09 in mid-2025 and has held at $0.08-0.10/lb even with copper at $6-6.50/lb. RBC expects further re-rating as permitting and de-risking progress.
RBC hosted 16 junior copper developers at its third annual Sparks Flying conference last week.
Implied copper price from the copper equities (each model set to 1.0x NAVPS, other commodities at spot) ranges from $3.60 to $5.89/lb across FCX, FM, LUN, CS, HBM and IVN, below spot copper.

Valuation context: North American copper producers trade at 0.8x P/NAV vs a 10Y average of 0.9x, and 6.9x EV/NTM EBITDA vs a 10Y average of 5.9x. Global diversifieds trade at 1.1x P/NAV and 6.2x EV/NTM EBITDA.
Estimates were fine-tuned for CIA, HBM, LIF and LUN. Ratings and price targets are unchanged: CIA Outperform C$8, HBM Outperform C$48, LIF Sector Perform C$36, LUN Sector Perform C$47.
RBC copper deck: $6.13/lb in 2026E, $6.00 in 2027E and 2028E, $5.00 long-term. Gold $4,532/oz in 2026E and $4,960 in 2027E. Iron ore $100.18/t in 2026E and $88.75 in 2027E.

sector_views.rationale: Copper equities fell 7% w/w on risk-off. RBC sees supply tightness in the physical market and a further re-rate for junior developers.
Prices are soft on weak steel demand and strong supply. Vale's CEO says ~160Mt of supply is unprofitable, which should support a recovery.

earnings_insights: RBC fine-tuned estimates for CIA, HBM, LIF and LUN, with no rating or target changes.
CIA: FY27E (FY Mar) adj. EBITDA C$663.2M (prev. C$705.7M), adj. diluted EPS C$0.42 (prev. C$0.46). Q2 FY27 EBITDA estimate is C$36.0E and Q3 is C$252.0E (prev. Q2 C$120.1E). FY28E EBITDA is C$968.0M.
HBM: 2026E adj. diluted EPS $2.07 and adj. EBITDA $1,578.5M (prev. $1,576.7M). Q3 2026E EPS is $0.41 (prev. $0.47) and Q4 is $0.44 (prev. $0.37). Q1 2026 EPS of $0.41 and Q2 of $0.28 are actuals.
LIF: 2026E adj. diluted EPS C$0.75, 2027E C$2.49 and 2028E C$2.23. Q3 2026E is C$0.17 (prev. C$0.18) and Q4 is C$0.15 (prev. C$0.19). Q1 C$0.21 and Q2 C$0.18 are actuals.

LUN: 2026E adj. diluted EPS $1.52 (prev. $1.54) and adj. EBITDA $2,870.6M (prev. $2,890.6M). Q3 2026E EPS is $0.36 (prev. $0.38). Q1 $0.33 and Q2 $0.30 are actuals. 2027E EPS is $1.60 and 2028E is $1.23.

Lundin catalysts: Q1 2027 Candelaria Franco-Nevada stream step-down from 68% to 40%, adding ~$56-90M in annual FCF. Vicuña FID in 2026. Ball mill commissioning at Chapada and Caserones in 2027. Saúva first ore in 2029.

macro_indicators.interpretation: RBC says the print weighed on sentiment for copper equities last week.
Spot copper was flat while copper equities fell 7%.
Singapore futures dipped below $90/t for the first time in two years, then firmed on seasonal steel demand.
RBC price deck used for NAVs and price targets.
Metal diverted to the US has tightened the physical market in Europe.

Iron ore: soft steel demand and strong supply pushed Singapore futures below $90/t.
Execution and financing risk at Lundin's Vicuña district alongside BHP.
Champion's single-asset concentration and lack of its own railway to port.
